structuredResult.summary: The smallest proposed architecture is the existing synchronized, in-memory `demo.LinkBook` domain model. Each reserved code owns one immutable destination, optional expiry, active state, lifetime count, and UTC-date count map. Resolution performs eligibility checks before recording, with expiry defined as `now >= expiresAt`; only successful `record=true` resolutions update both counters atomically. Disable and delete retain the record so its code and analytics remain preserved. No HTTP, database, external dependency, destination fetch, or deployment component is warranted. The supplied implementation appears structurally aligned with this design, but actual Maven verification remains an execution gate.
risks: “Permanent” is domain permanence within the lifetime of this in-memory fixture, not durability across process restarts; persistence is explicitly outside scope.
The source may require no engineering change, but that conclusion must remain provisional until the unchanged combined candidate is independently checked with `mvn verify`.
Any future refactor could incorrectly separate eligibility checking from counter updates, allowing failed, HEAD, or concurrent resolutions to corrupt analytics.
Changing the UTC conversion, equality boundary, destination string, supplied acceptance tests, dependency versions, or `pom.xml` verification behavior would violate the approved contract.
A domain-only fixture must not be represented as demonstrating a complete REST or persistent shortener service.

tasks.description: Using the declared requirements evidence, README contract, supplied acceptance tests, current `LinkBook` implementation, and fixture POM as inputs, produce an architecture artifact under `artifacts/architecture/` that records the minimal in-memory design and proposed downstream task graph. Specify immutable destinations; permanently retained code records; nullable expiry with `now >= expiresAt`; synchronized eligibility-and-recording behavior; lifetime and UTC daily counters; count preservation after disable/delete; zero analytics for unknown codes; and no counting for HEAD or failed resolutions. The proposed graph must preserve the fixture POM and acceptance tests, limit implementation work to `LinkBook` only if a behavioral gap is found, allow focused supplementary test work after the shared contract, and join all changes at a final `mvn verify` gate without claiming that gate has passed.

structuredResult.summary: Requirements are fully clarified for the supplied LinkBook fixture. “Permanent” means each code remains permanently reserved, including after deletion, and its destination never changes; links may optionally expire, with expiration beginning when now equals expiresAt. A resolution succeeds only for an existing, active, non-deleted, non-expired link. Analytics count only successful resolutions with record=true: expose a lifetime total and UTC-calendar-day counts based on the supplied resolution instant. record=false (HEAD), missing links, expired links, disabled links, and deleted links do not increment analytics. Disabling or deleting a link preserves its existing counts. Unknown codes report zero. Preserve the fixture pom.xml and supplied acceptance tests. Scope excludes an HTTP server, persistence system, destination fetch, external dependencies, deployment, and changes outside artifacts/requirements/.
risks: “Permanent” must not be interpreted as forcing every link to be non-expiring; optional expiry remains supported.
Analytics represent recorded successful resolutions, not verified visits to or successful fetches from destination URLs.
The fixture is in-memory, so counts and reserved codes are not durable across process restarts; durable storage is explicitly outside scope.
Boundary implementations can accidentally count HEAD or failed resolutions, or treat expiresAt equality as still valid.
Normalizing or rewriting destination strings would violate the fixed-destination requirement.
The supplied implementation appears aligned with the clarified observable behavior, but no independent Maven verification is claimed.

tasks.description: Record the approved fixture requirements and observable acceptance criteria in a requirements artifact: immutable destinations; permanently reserved unique codes, including deleted codes; nullable expiry; expiration at now >= expiresAt; empty resolution for missing, expired, disabled, or deleted links; counting only successful record=true resolutions; lifetime totals and UTC daily buckets; count preservation after disable/delete; and zero counts for unknown codes. State the explicit exclusions and preservation constraints for pom.xml and supplied acceptance tests.
